# castsnap field reference

What every dataset, file and field in a castsnap export means, in plain words. Each meaning says what it rests on.

docs/fields.json and docs/FIELDS.md hold no values from real exports. Any example value is invented and labeled as an example.

In this reference, "you", "your" and "yours" mean the exported account. A private export is always of the session token's own account, since castsnap refuses a --fid that differs from it. A public export can be of any account.

## Contents

- [Bases](#bases)
- [Statuses](#statuses)
- [Datasets](#datasets)
- [Files](#files)
- [Printed lines](#printed-lines)

## Bases

Each description ends with its basis: where its meaning comes from.

- **From castsnap's code** (`code`): castsnap writes or computes it, so its meaning is known from castsnap's own code and docs.
- **The app's own description** (`app`): The Farcaster app describes it in its own text. castsnap copies it and does not interpret it.
- **Inferred** (`inferred`): The app does not document it. The meaning is inferred, and the entry says from what: the web app's code, or its name only.
- **From a documented source** (`docs`): The Farcaster protocol's published definitions, linked from the entry.
- **Not known** (`unknown`): Only its name is known, and the name supports no meaning.

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `complete` | Every source for the dataset finished without an error. Usually that means each paged source reached its last page; for D19 and D20 it can also mean castsnap stopped at its page cap, and then the source's note says so. |
| `empty` | The sources answered and held nothing. |
| `unavailable:<reason>` | The data could not be fetched, for the reason given, such as `unavailable:private-not-requested` without --private. |
| `error:<reason>` | Fetching failed. When a lane stops early, the datasets it never reached are `error:<lane>-lane-aborted`. |
| `interrupted` | Ctrl-C stopped the run before the dataset was finished. |

### D19. Your own moderation record

State: exported. Needs --private: yes.

- What the app shows an account it has moderated out, on that account's own profile, behind a feature flag. (Basis: inferred from the web app's code)
- castsnap fetches it from `GET /v2/network-code/public-rap-sheet`, asked with your token for your own account only, 20 per page, up to 100 pages. castsnap asks on every --private run and keeps the pages as they came, without normalizing them. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- Its count adds up the lists directly under `result` on each page. It is empty (null) when a page's result has fields but no list. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- If pages remain after the 100th, castsnap stops there, still marks the dataset `complete`, and adds a note that the next cursor was not followed. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- Information only: it never makes the export fail, and verify shows it on its STATUS line without grading it. Its counts are personal; sharing them is your choice. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

Files:

- [`raw/client/moderation-record/page-NNNN.json`](#rawclientmoderation-recordpage-nnnnjson)
- [`raw/client/moderation-record/error-NNNN.json`](#rawclientmoderation-recorderror-nnnnjson)

Sources in manifest.json: `client:moderation-record`.

Sources: `docs/SPEC.md`.

### D20. The stayed list

State: exported. Needs --private: yes.

- What the app shows with its opt-in agreement: a count and the first few accounts. (Basis: inferred from the web app's code)
- The reading that these are accounts you follow that have stayed, meaning they accepted the agreement, rests only on the request's path, `/v2/opt-in/following-stayed`, and on the name of the part of the app that shows it. (Basis: inferred from the web app's code)
- castsnap asks once, with your token, and keeps the answer as it came. Its count is `result.count` when that is a number, otherwise the number of `result.users`. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- castsnap asks for one page only. If the answer points to a next page, castsnap doesn't follow it, still marks the dataset `complete`, and adds a note saying so. Information only: it never makes the export fail. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

Files:

- [`raw/client/following-stayed/page-0001.json`](#rawclientfollowing-stayedpage-0001json)
- [`raw/client/following-stayed/error-0001.json`](#rawclientfollowing-stayederror-0001json)

Sources in manifest.json: `client:following-stayed`.

Sources: `docs/SPEC.md`.

## Files

### `raw/protocol/signers-by-fid.jsonl`

Signer list, raw. Datasets: D7.

- One line per page of the node's signer list for your account, each the Farcaster library's JSON form of the node's answer. Bytes are base64 text, enum values are their names, and 64-bit numbers are plain numbers. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- It lists gasless keys as well as on-chain keys. normalized/signers.json lists on-chain key events only. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| Field | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signers` | list | The keys on this page. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, SignersByFidResponse](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) |
| `signers[].source` | text | Where the key came from, by name: `SIGNER_SOURCE_ONCHAIN` for a key added on-chain, `SIGNER_SOURCE_OFFCHAIN` for a gasless key added by a KEY_ADD message. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509), [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L477-L481) |
| `signers[].key` | bytes (base64) | The key: a 32-byte Ed25519 public key. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].keyType` | number | The key's type, as a number: 1 means Ed25519. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].fid` | number | The account the key belongs to. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].addedAt` | number (Unix seconds), optional | When the key was added. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].lastUsedAt` | number (Unix seconds), optional | Gasless keys only: when the key was last used. Present when the node provides it; whether nodes fill it is unverified. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].ttl` | number (seconds), optional | Gasless keys only: how long the key stays valid after its last use. The window slides: each use moves the expiry forward. Present when the node provides it; whether nodes fill it is unverified. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509), [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/protocol/discussions/266) |
| `signers[].expiresAt` | number (Unix seconds), optional | lastUsedAt plus ttl, when ttl is above 0. Present when the node provides it; whether nodes fill it is unverified. verify works out expiry offline instead. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509), `src/gasless.ts` |
| `signers[].scopes` | list of numbers | Gasless keys only: the message types the key may sign, as numbers from the protocol's MessageType list. A message from that key whose type isn't listed fails validation. On-chain keys carry no scopes, so for them the list is empty. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509), [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/protocol/discussions/266) |
| `signers[].requestFid` | number, optional | Gasless keys only: the FID of the app that requested the key, as verified from the key request's signed metadata. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].nonce` | number, optional | Gasless keys only: the user nonce on the KEY_ADD that added the key. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `signers[].onchainEvent` | object, optional | On-chain keys only: the original on-chain event that added the key. (This covers everything under it.) | [Snapchain request_response.proto, Signer](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L485-L509) |
| `nextPageToken` | bytes (base64) | Where the next page starts; castsnap stops when it is empty. | from castsnap's code | `src/protocol/grpc.ts#GrpcTransport`, `src/export.ts#runExport` |
| `gaslessSignerCount` | number | The account's active gasless keys. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, SignersByFidResponse](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) |
| `gaslessSignerLimit` | number | The cap on active gasless keys per account. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, SignersByFidResponse](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) |
| `currentUserNonce` | number | The highest user nonce accepted on a KEY_ADD or a custody-signed KEY_REMOVE, or 0 when there has been none. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, SignersByFidResponse](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) |
| `requesterFidNonces` | object | A map from a requesting app's FID to that app's current nonce, with one entry for each FID the request asked about. castsnap's request asks about none, so in this version's exports it is always an empty object. | [Snapchain request_response.proto, SignersByFidResponse](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553) | [link](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/request_response.proto#L531-L553), `src/protocol/grpc.ts#GrpcTransport` |

Sources: `src/export.ts#runExport`.

### `raw/protocol/key-messages.jsonl`

Key messages, raw. Datasets: D7.

- Your KEY_ADD and KEY_REMOVE messages, found by searching the node's blocks, one per line in time order. Each is the Farcaster library's JSON form of the message. Bytes are base64 text, enum values are their names, and 64-bit numbers are plain numbers. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- A KEY_ADD (message type 16) adds a key through a message carrying the custody address's signature, with no on-chain transaction. A KEY_REMOVE (17) revokes a key. (Basis: [Snapchain message.proto, message types 16 and 17](https://github.com/farcasterxyz/snapchain/blob/1405794471d7edf701e3f93658e0f600ef3b112b/proto/definitions/message.proto#L87-L88))

| Field | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### `raw/client/moderation-record/error-NNNN.json`

Moderation record, refused or unreadable answer. Datasets: D19.

- Written when the app refuses a page (an HTTP status other than 200) and sends a body, or answers with something that isn't JSON or has no `result`. It holds the app's answer cut to its first 2,000 characters, then with any copy of your token replaced by `[REDACTED]`. Its number follows the last good page. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- It may not parse as JSON: the answer may not have been JSON, and the cut can fall partway through. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

No fields are described: see the lines above.

Sources: `src/export.ts#runExport`.

### `media/index.jsonl`

Media index. Datasets: D14.

- One JSON object per line, one per distinct embed URL: from your own casts, from your bookmarks, or both, as --media chooses. Written whenever --media includes own or bookmarks. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- castsnap follows redirects itself, one hop at a time and at most 5. Before the first request and each redirect, it refuses a scheme other than http and https, a host named localhost or ending in .localhost, and a host that is or resolves to a loopback, private, shared (100.64.0.0/10), link-local, unique-local, multicast, reserved (240.0.0.0/4) or unspecified address. It stores an image, video, audio file or PDF under media/sha256/, named by its SHA-256; other content is listed but not stored. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| Field | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | text | The embed URL, as the cast gives it. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `castHashes` | list | The casts that embed this URL. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `castHashes[]` | hex text | A cast's hash, as hex. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia`, `src/export.ts#runExport` |
| `origins` | list | Where the URL was found. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `origins[]` | text | `own` for your own casts, `bookmark` for a bookmarked cast. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia`, `src/export.ts#runExport` |
| `status` | number or null | The final HTTP status, after any redirects. null when there was no response; then `error` says why. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `finalUrl` | text, optional | The URL that gave the final response, when redirects led away from `url`. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `contentType` | text, optional | The final response's Content-Type header, as given. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `kind` | text | image, video, audio, document or other. From the content type of a 200 response; otherwise from the URL's file extension and a few known image and video hosts. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#kindOf`, `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `bytes` | number, optional | The stored file's size in bytes. Present only when `stored` is true. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |
| `sha256` | hex text, optional | The stored file's SHA-256, as hex in lower case. Present only when `stored` is true. | from castsnap's code | `src/media.ts#downloadMedia` |

### `reconciliation.json`

Reconciliation. Datasets: none.

- Compares what the protocol nodes hold with the app's lists and profile: following, followers, blocks and five profile fields. Each difference is an entry with a reason code from a closed list. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- A list castsnap couldn't get from the app isn't compared; the profile is compared only when castsnap has the app's profile. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- The file is checked against its schema, normalized/schemas/reconciliation.schema.json. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| Field | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | number | The version of this file's layout. Always 1 in this version of castsnap. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `fid` | number | The FID of the exported account. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `reasonCodes` | list of text | Every reason code an entry can have: self_follow, hidden_by_client, client_only, count_mismatch and profile_field_mismatch. | from castsnap's code | `src/schemas.ts#REASON_CODES`, `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `summary` | object | Counts for each comparison. following: protocol (the protocol set's size), selfFollow, protocolExcludingSelf, clientList (the app list's length), profileFollowingCount, countMatchesProfile, protocolOnly and clientOnly. followers: protocol, clientList, profileFollowerCount, protocolOnly, clientOnly and clientOnlyTolerance (the larger of 2 and 0.5% of the app list's length). blocks: protocol, clientList, protocolOnly and clientOnly. Each is null when its input is missing. profile: fieldsCompared (username, displayName, bio, pfpUrl and url), clientAvailable and mismatches (the fields that differ). entriesByReason: the number of entries for each reason code. (This covers everything under it.) | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries` | list | The differences: following's first, then followers', blocks' and the profile's. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[]` | object | One difference. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].dataset` | text | Which comparison found it: following, followers, blocks or profile. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].reason` | text | Its reason code. self_follow: the protocol has the exported account following itself, and the app's list doesn't include it. hidden_by_client: the protocol set has the account, and the app's list doesn't. client_only: the app's list has the account, and the protocol set doesn't. count_mismatch: the protocol following count, not counting a self-follow, differs from the profile's followingCount. profile_field_mismatch: a profile field differs between the protocol and the app. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].fid` | number, optional | The FID of the account the difference is about. On self_follow, hidden_by_client and client_only entries. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].field` | text, optional | The profile field that differs. On profile_field_mismatch entries. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].protocol` | any value, optional | The protocol side: the following count without a self-follow, on count_mismatch; the field's latest protocol value as text, or empty text when unset, on profile_field_mismatch. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].client` | any value, optional | The app's side: the profile's followingCount, on count_mismatch; the app's value as text, or empty text when absent, on profile_field_mismatch. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |
| `entries[].detail` | text, optional | A plain description of the comparison. On count_mismatch entries. | from castsnap's code | `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile` |

Sources: `src/reconcile.ts#reconcile`, `src/schemas.ts#RECONCILIATION_SCHEMA`, `src/export.ts#runExport`.

### `raw/client/muted-keywords/error-0001.json`

Muted keywords, refused or unreadable answer. Datasets: D12.

- Written when the request ends without a JSON answer with HTTP status 200: the app refuses it (any other status), answers with something that isn't JSON, or no answer arrives. It holds the answer cut to its first 4,000 characters, then with any copy of your token replaced by `[REDACTED]`. When no answer arrives (the network still fails after castsnap's retries, or castsnap refuses to send the token to that host), the file is written empty. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- It may not parse as JSON: the answer may not have been JSON, and the cut can fall partway through. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

### `raw/client/bookmarks/error-NNNN.json`

Bookmarks, refused page or no answer. Datasets: D3.

- Written when a page's request gets an HTTP status other than 200, or no answer arrives; castsnap stops there. A first page refused with 400 is asked again with a smaller limit first, and only the last refusal is written. It holds the answer cut to its first 2,000 characters, then with any copy of your token replaced by `[REDACTED]`. When no answer arrives (the network still fails after castsnap's retries, or castsnap refuses to send the token to that host), the file is written empty. Its number follows the last page written. No error file is written when the source ends any other way: complete; `empty`, when the last page is reached and no page held an item; stopped at a page it keeps (one that isn't JSON, a first page without the list, or a repeated cursor); interrupted; or failed inside castsnap. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- It may not parse as JSON: the answer may not have been JSON, and the cut can fall partway through. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

No fields are described: see the lines above.

Sources: `src/export.ts#runExport`, `src/client.ts#ClientApi.paginate`, `src/client.ts#ClientApi.get`.

### `raw/client/dm-conversations-CATEGORY/error-NNNN.json`

Direct-cast conversation lists, refused page or no answer. Datasets: D10.

- Written when a page's request gets an HTTP status other than 200, or no answer arrives; castsnap stops there. A first page refused with 400 is asked again with a smaller limit first, and only the last refusal is written. It holds the answer cut to its first 2,000 characters, then with any copy of your token replaced by `[REDACTED]`. When no answer arrives (the network still fails after castsnap's retries, or castsnap refuses to send the token to that host), the file is written empty. Its number follows the last page written. No error file is written when the source ends any other way: complete; `empty`, when the last page is reached and no page held an item; stopped at a page it keeps (one that isn't JSON, a first page without the list, or a repeated cursor); interrupted; or failed inside castsnap. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- It may not parse as JSON: the answer may not have been JSON, and the cut can fall partway through. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- CATEGORY is the list the pages come from: `default`, `archived`, `request` or `void`. castsnap reads all four, in that order. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

No fields are described: see the lines above.

Sources: `src/export.ts#runExport`, `src/client.ts#ClientApi.paginate`, `src/client.ts#ClientApi.get`.

### `raw/client/dm-messages/NNNN-ID/page-NNNN.json`

Direct-cast messages, raw pages. Datasets: D10.

- One file per page, numbered from 0001: the app's answer listing the messages in one of your direct-cast conversations, exactly as it came. Written on --private runs. The fields below are the ones castsnap reads; anything else on the page is kept but not described. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- castsnap asks for 50 items a page; if the app refuses the first page with HTTP 400, it asks again for 15, then with no limit. It follows `next.cursor` until a page has none. A page that isn't JSON is still kept, and the source stops there with `error:non-json`; so does a first page with no list under `messages`, with `error:missing-messages`, and a page whose `next.cursor` was seen before, with `error:cursor-loop`. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- Each conversation castsnap kept from the lists has its own folder, fetched in the order of its `index`. The folder's name is that `index` from normalized/dm-conversations.json, padded with zeros to at least four digits, a hyphen, then the conversation's ID with every character other than A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `.`, `_` and `-` replaced by `_`, cut to 80 characters. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- The messages source is one source for all conversations. When any conversation's messages don't end `complete` or `empty`, its status is `error:<n>-conversations-not-complete`, with n the number of those conversations, unless the run was interrupted. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| `result.messages[]` | object, optional | One message. Every item gives a record, with the conversation's `conversationId`, even when it has none of the fields below. | from castsnap's code | `src/export.ts#runExport`, `src/normalize.ts#dmMessageRecord` |

## Printed lines

### The account-status line

Printed by:

- export: after its Datasets line
- auth-check: after its OK line, built from `/v2/me`, so without publicSpamLabel
- verify: in its STATUS entry, rebuilt from the saved pages, followed by the D19 and D20 counts and the words information only: not graded
- quick capture: before its Files line

- One line saying how the Farcaster app treats your account right now. castsnap copies what the app sent and does not interpret it. The line is safe to share. (Basis: from castsnap's code)
- A plain word is shown as it is; anything else is shown as JSON, cut at 120 characters. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| Part | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optInStatus` | text | A status the app checks. The web app's code checks for the values `pending` and `moderated_out`, among others that can occur. | inferred from the web app's code | `src/status.ts#statusFromProfile`, `src/status.ts#statusFromMe` |
| `publicSpamLabel` | text | From its name: a spam label the app shows publicly for the account. Printed only when the line comes from a profile answer, because `/v2/me` has none. | inferred from its name only | `src/status.ts#statusLine` |
| `nerfed` | true or false | Printed only when the app's answer has it. The app describes a nerfed account as one that can still post to the protocol but does not appear in the Farcaster app. | the app's own description | `src/status.ts#statusLine` |
| `(not reported)` | marker | The app's answer had no such field. | from castsnap's code | `src/status.ts#statusLine` |
| `not available` | marker | castsnap had no readable answer to build the line from. | from castsnap's code | `src/status.ts#statusLine` |
| `from` | label | Which saved answer the line comes from: `profile-after` (the profile fetched at the end of the run, preferred), `profile-before` (at the start), `me` (the token check, --private runs only), or `/v2/me` in auth-check. | from castsnap's code | `src/status.ts#pickStatus`, `src/cli.ts` |
| `canSendDirectCasts` | true or false | Kept in manifest.json, not printed. From its name: whether the one viewing can send this account a direct cast. castsnap fetches the profile without a token, so that viewer is anonymous. | inferred from its name only | `src/status.ts#statusFromProfile` |
| `neynarScore` | number | Kept in manifest.json on --private runs, not printed. From its name: a score attached to your account. Its scale and use are not documented. | inferred from its name only | `src/status.ts#statusFromMe` |
| `enabledFeatureFlags` | list of text | Kept in manifest.json on --private runs, not printed. From its name: app features switched on for your account. | inferred from its name only | `src/status.ts#statusFromMe` |

Sources: `src/status.ts#statusLine`.

### The Privacy: line

Printed by:

- export: near the start of the run, after the Account: and Token: lines

- One line, printed by export, saying whether the new export folder can be read by your account only, how castsnap set that, and what kind of place the folder is in. The same facts are kept in manifest.json under `privacy`. (Basis: from castsnap's code)

| Part | Type | Meaning | Basis | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readable by your account only` | text | castsnap set the export folder's permissions to owner-only, then read them back, and what it read back was owner-only. | from castsnap's code | `src/permissions.ts#makeOwnerOnly` |
| `NOT limited to your account` | text | Setting the permissions failed, or what castsnap read back still lets other accounts in. Other accounts on this computer may be able to read the folder. | from castsnap's code | `src/permissions.ts#makeOwnerOnly` |
| `method` | label | In brackets: how castsnap set the permissions, `posix-mode` (file modes, on macOS and Linux) or `windows-acl` (access lists, on Windows; hands-on test pending). | from castsnap's code | `src/permissions.ts#makeOwnerOnly` |
| `location` | label | After `location:`, the label as printed: a short fixed description of where the folder is, such as `a local folder`, `a OneDrive folder` or `a network mount`. Never a path or a volume name. | from castsnap's code | `src/location.ts` |
| `, allowed by --allow-unsafe-location` | text | Added when the location check would have refused the folder and --allow-unsafe-location let the run go ahead. | from castsnap's code | `src/export.ts#runExport` |

Sources: `src/export.ts#runExport`.
